newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stealth jets to depart for Gulf today.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stealth jets to depart for Gulf today.

text.p: Eight U.S. F-117A "stealth" fighters will leave Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico, within hours for a base in the Gulf to prepare for possible air strikes against Iraq, U.S. defence officials said on Thursday.
The radar-avoiding jets will make a long, non-stop flight to Kuwait after a planned departure at about 2 p.m. New Mexico time (2000 GMT), arriving in Kuwait late on Friday.
The Pentagon refused to say where the jets were going, but administration officials said on Wednesday that Kuwait had agreed to base the jets there.
Air Force officials said U.S. aerial refueling tanker planes would accompany the F-117As and refuel them in the air as they make a non-stop flight of nearly 20 hours.
Big KC-135 tankers from McConnell Air Force in Wichita, Kansas, and KC-10 tankers from McGuire AFB in New Jersey will refuel the planes during the trip, the officials said.
In Baghdad, Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz warned Kuwait on Thursday against permitting U.S. warplanes to use its territory for possible military strikes against targets in Iraq.

The United States has also based B-52 bombers at a British air base on the island of Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean in preparation for possible raids on Iraq as tensions escalate between Washington and Baghdad.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Wednesday the United States had not asked Saudi Arabia to accept the stealth fighters, which use a bat-wing design and composite construction materials to make them almost invisible to radar.

The Stealth jets were based in Saudi Arabia during the 1991 Gulf War and used with devastating accuracy against Iraqi targets. They fly slower than the speed of sound, but drop laser-guided 2,000-pound (908 kg) bombs which can hit concrete Iraqi air defence command-and-control centres and other targets with high accuracy.
